Unlike the October absence (AR-009), this extended claim is not independently cross-checked against those specific agendas by any other document in this case - it is carried in the same source that also supplies Account Two's uncorroborated resolution numbers (AR-006).
determinations: The extended multi-cycle absence claim should be treated with the same caution as Account Two's resolution numbers - plausible and consistent with the confirmed October absence, but not independently verified meeting-by-meeting the way the October absence is.
paths.boundary: Does not dispute the claim - only notes it has not received the same cross-source confirmation as the October absence specifically.

paths.title: The 18 March 2026 Council Letter — Item-by-Item Content Analysis
analysis: Council's letter to Bellbrook residents, signed by Caro Szary, Group Manager Strategic and Asset Planning (EV-0004), makes six distinct claims of activity: (1) correspondence to NSW DCCEEW, (2) correspondence to Mid North Coast Local Health District, (3) the 2025 community meeting, (4) the September 2025 door-knocking, (5) ongoing camp monitoring, (6) a letter of support to Bellbrook Public School, and states an intention to (7) seek external grants and (8) request state-level support via Michael Kemp MP.

Of these eight items, two are independently cross-referenced elsewhere in this case's chronology (the community meeting, CHR-0004; the door-knocking, CHR-0005). The remaining six - both correspondence items, the monitoring, the school letter, and both stated intentions - are described only in this one letter, not independently sighted or corroborated by any other document.
determinations: The letter documents a real and specific set of activities, two of which have independent chronological corroboration - but discloses no outcome for any of the eight items, and no commitment to the one instrument (a management plan) this case's central finding identifies as the actual funding precondition (AR-002).
paths.boundary: Does not claim the six uncorroborated items are false - only that they rest on Council's own account alone, which is a different evidentiary status than the two chronologically cross-referenced items.

paths.title: Level 1/Level 2 Management Actions Under the Code of Practice
analysis: The NSW Flying-fox Camp Management Code of Practice 2018 pre-approves certain Level 1 (routine site management, hygiene cleaning, signage) and Level 2 (vegetation buffer creation, branch trimming) interventions without individual licensing, subject to welfare-based scheduling conditions such as trimming only after animals depart to forage (EV-0012). Protected-species status prevents dispersal or lethal control of the colony itself; it is described as not preventing these specific lower-tier actions.
determinations: Legal protection of the species does not, on this description, by itself explain an absence of any interim Level 1/Level 2 action at the site.
paths.boundary: This description has not yet been checked against the primary Code of Practice text itself (Q-0007) - it rests on two cross-corroborating but secondary operator-supplied documents, not a directly-sighted regulatory instrument.

paths.title: The Operator's Commonwealth Registration Attempt
analysis: On 18 June 2026 at 9:56am, the operator emailed speciespolicy@dcceew.gov.au, cc'ing Paul Hodgson (the same Bellbrook Hall and Progress Association member named in EV-0001), formally notifying the Department of the Bellbrook camp and requesting assistance arranging a formal species count/census (EV-0022). The operator separately confirmed this was a deliberate registration attempt, made after learning any member of the public could submit one. This is the case's first confirmed-sent advocacy action with a dated send record, distinct from the four still-unconfirmed drafted submissions (see AR-021).
determinations: This is the only advocacy action in this case's register with both a confirmed send date and a confirmed substantive reply - a materially different evidentiary category from any of the four drafted-but-unconfirmed submissions.
paths.boundary: Does not itself establish anything about the camp's registration status - only that the attempt was made and dated.

paths.title: DCCEEW's Reply — Substantive Content Analysis
analysis: DCCEEW's direct reply (Sam Horton, Senior Policy Officer, Species Listing, Information and Policy Section, EV-0023) makes four distinct claims: (1) the National Flying Fox Monitoring Program was a collaboration between national, state/territory governments, CSIRO, local governments and community volunteers; (2) it was paused in 2022 due to cessation of federal funding; (3) the Department is not currently monitoring flying-fox camps under it and cannot send resources to survey the Bellbrook camp; (4) grey-headed flying-foxes remain federally protected, and any camp exceeding the 'nationally important camp' threshold would still need referral, with a recommendation to engage the relevant state government instead.
This is a primary institutional source responding directly to a dated, confirmed action by this case's own operator - the single hardest fact in the entire register.
determinations: The Commonwealth camp-registration/monitoring pathway is confirmed non-functional for a new camp via this specific route, independent of anything Kempsey Shire Council has or has not done - grounded in direct institutional correspondence, not inference.
paths.boundary: Does not establish whether Bellbrook meets the 'nationally important camp' threshold that would trigger referral regardless of the pause - see AR-015.

paths.title: The EPBC 'Nationally Important Camp' Threshold — Unresolved
analysis: DCCEEW's reply (EV-0023) states that a camp exceeding the EPBC Act's 'nationally important camp' threshold would still require referral, independent of the paused monitoring program. Nothing in this case's register establishes the size, density, or any other threshold-relevant characteristic of the Bellbrook colony against that specific test.
determinations: This is a genuinely open, distinct question from the monitoring-program pause (AR-014) - a live referral obligation could exist regardless of the pause, and this case's register currently contains no basis to assess it either way.
paths.boundary: Q-0011 remains fully open. This path does not speculate about the likely outcome of an assessment this case has no data to perform.

paths.title: The 'Historic' Classification Claim
analysis: The media pitch document states Council's website classifies Bellbrook as a 'historic' flying-fox camp (EV-0009) - a single-source claim when first recorded, not repeated in any of the other seven original documents. Later operator-relayed research (EV-0016) restates this and adds that Rudder Park is described as Council's only permanent camp and that Council states it cannot manage colonies on private or Crown land - with partial independent corroboration via an unrelated search snippet (found while searching NSW Parliament Hansard on a different query) that consistently used the words 'historic flying-fox camp location'.
determinations: The 'historic' classification claim has moved from single-source (EV-0009) to partially independently corroborated (EV-0016) across this case's runs - but 'partially corroborated by an unrelated search' is a materially weaker evidentiary status than a direct, dated sighting of the page itself.
paths.boundary: Does not establish whether the classification is currently accurate or stale - see AR-018 for the real, confirmed 2021 departure that provides a plausible innocent explanation this path does not rule out.

paths.title: The Unlocated June 2026 Severity Report
analysis: Operator-relayed research states a June 2026 report described the Bellbrook camp as severely affecting residents - the park reportedly unusable, waste affecting public areas, impacts on Bellbrook Public School children, residents still seeking intervention (EV-0015). An extensive independent search across the Macleay Argus, ABC Mid North Coast, Mirage News, NSW Parliament Hansard and the June 2026 Kempsey council meeting wrap found no trace of it.
determinations: This claim cannot currently be treated as established - not because it has been contradicted, but because this case has been unable to locate the source it is attributed to despite a genuine, multi-source search attempt.
paths.boundary: Non-location is not disproof. If the operator can supply the specific citation, this path should be revisited in a later pass rather than the claim being treated as settled either way in the meantime.

paths.title: The 2021 Departure Record and Chronology Coherence
analysis: Council's own 27 October 2021 page reports the colony left Bellbrook that year as weather warmed, with Bellbrook Playground subsequently cleaned and reopened; the article also states Council was aware of impacts earlier that year but could not interfere with the colony due to its protected status (EV-0013). This was independently found while attempting to verify the 'historic' classification claim, and was not previously in this case's register.

This complicates, rather than confirms or refutes, the case's own working framing that the colony has been 'continuous since November 2019' (CHR-0001). If the colony genuinely left in 2021 and only later returned, that is a materially different history than uninterrupted presence - and would provide a real, non-inaccurate basis for a 'historic' classification, if the colony has not since returned.
determinations: This case's own chronology (CHR-0001's 'continuous since 2019' framing) and this independently-found record (a confirmed 2021 departure) are not yet reconciled - this is an internal coherence gap in the case's own record, not merely an external dispute with Council.
paths.boundary: Does not determine whether the colony returned after 2021, or when. Q-0008 remains open.

paths.title: Histoplasmosis Mechanism — Real, Unconfirmed Locally
analysis: Histoplasmosis, a fungal lung/bloodstream infection from inhaling spores in accumulated droppings, is described as a real, medically documented mechanism under heavy direct droppings accumulation - distinguishable from the standard 'low risk from a distance' messaging calibrated for colonies without direct droppings contact (EV-0008). The source document explicitly notes no lab test has confirmed Histoplasma capsulatum in this specific colony's droppings, and that an absence of confirmed local cases does not mean no mild or undiagnosed infections have occurred, citing literature suggesting undiagnosed rates as high as 90% in immunocompetent people.
determinations: A real, medically documented health-risk mechanism exists in principle for heavy direct droppings exposure; no local case is confirmed, and the source material itself explicitly frames this as a scope limitation rather than a claim about anyone's intent.
paths.boundary: Must not be read as evidence any Bellbrook resident has been sickened - the source item and this path both explicitly limit the claim to mechanism, not confirmed instance (Q-0006).

paths.title: ABLV Bite/Scratch Mechanism — Real, Unconfirmed Locally, Distinct Pathway
analysis: Australian bat lyssavirus (ABLV) is a real, medically serious bite/scratch transmission risk - potentially fatal, causing paralysis, delirium and convulsions, with four deaths recorded nationally since 1996 (EV-0018, reporting a rise in North Queensland exposures, flagged by the operator as relevant background rather than a Bellbrook-specific claim). Mid North Coast Local Health District's own general public health guidance independently confirms the standard precautions: avoid handling injured or dead flying foxes, contact wildlife rescue services, wash any bite/scratch wound for 15 minutes and seek immediate medical attention (EV-0019, the only ABLV-related item in this case independently fetched and read in full).
determinations: This is a distinct exposure pathway and disease from the droppings-based histoplasmosis risk (AR-019) - different mechanism, different route, same underlying point: a real medical risk exists independent of any confirmed local case, and the two should not be conflated into one generic 'health risk' finding.
paths.boundary: EV-0018 is not Bellbrook-, Kempsey- or even NSW-specific - North Queensland exposure circumstances differ from Bellbrook's documented droppings-contamination concern. This case has no evidence of any Bellbrook-specific bite or scratch exposure (Q-0010).

paths.title: The Four Drafted-but-Unconfirmed Advocacy Submissions
analysis: Four formal documents were drafted for simultaneous lodgement, all with unsigned "Resident of Bellbrook NSW 2440" signature blocks as at case creation: a council submission with five direct questions to CEO Andrew Meddle (EV-0006), an NSW Ombudsman complaint under the Ombudsman Act 1974 (EV-0007), and a senator letter and media pitch referenced in the same drafting round. None has a confirmed lodgement date or any confirmed response in this case's register.
determinations: These four documents represent the advocacy chain's intended next step, not a completed action - a materially different evidentiary category from the operator's own confirmed-sent, confirmed-answered Commonwealth registration email (AR-013).
paths.boundary: Does not assume the four drafts were never sent - only that this case's register does not confirm they were (Q-0005).

paths.title: Evidentiary Weight Distribution Across the Register
analysis: Of the 23 evidence items in this case's frozen register, 5 are independently confirmed Verified (EV-0001, EV-0018, EV-0019, EV-0020, EV-0021). The remaining 18 are Requires Verification/Unverified, and within that group the sourcing itself varies materially: some are cross-corroborated across multiple operator-supplied documents (e.g. EV-0002, EV-0011, EV-0012), some rest on a single operator-supplied document (EV-0008, EV-0009), and four (EV-0013 aside, which is independently found and Verified-adjacent in method though formally Requires Verification) rest on operator-relayed research supplied without a citation as at the point of recording (EV-0014, EV-0015, EV-0016, and in part EV-0017).
determinations: This case's evidentiary base is not uniform in reliability even within the shared 'Requires Verification' label - treating every Unverified item as interchangeable would itself be a form of the generic flattening this analysis is built to avoid.
paths.boundary: This is a meta-analytical observation about the register's own composition, not a new factual finding about Bellbrook or Council.

paths.title: Three Accounts of Colony Continuity, Not One
analysis: This case's working chronology (CHR-0001) states the colony relocated to Bellbrook in November 2019 and treats its presence since then as continuous. Three source documents describe a materially different history when read closely. Account A (EV-0001, most documents): colony present since November 2019, no departure mentioned. Account B (EV-0013, independently found): Council's own 27 October 2021 page reports the colony left Bellbrook that year, with the playground subsequently cleaned. Account C (EV-0010, the Hardened Submission Package): the colony 'occupied central Bellbrook Park beginning December 2019' (a different month than every other source), then states 'following a temporary departure, the colony returned to the park in mid-2022 with a materially increased population size.'

Account C does not cite a source for the December 2019 start date, the temporary departure, or the mid-2022 return, and none of these three specific claims appears anywhere else in this case's register. It is nonetheless the same document that supplies Account Two of the meeting dispute (AR-006) and the specific resolution numbers this case treats with the most caution - so Account C's colony-continuity claims should receive at least the same level of caution.
determinations: This case's register now contains three non-identical accounts of the colony's continuity, not the single 'continuous since November 2019' fact CHR-0001 currently states as settled. Account B (the 2021 departure) is Council's own primary source and the most independently grounded of the three; Account C (temporary departure, mid-2022 return) is uncited and internally uncorroborated; Account A (simple continuity) is the majority framing but does not address either departure claim.
paths.boundary: Does not determine which account is accurate, or whether Accounts B and C describe the same event (a 2021 departure with a mid-2022 return would be consistent with both) or two different events. CHR-0001's 'continuous since November 2019' framing should not be treated as more settled than this three-way discrepancy allows. Recommend a future DFAPTI pass reconcile the chronology or log a new contradiction if the operator confirms these are genuinely in tension.

paths.title: The Defeated 2/7 Amendment — What It Actually Proposed
analysis: EV-0010's register summary records only that an amendment 'linking Bellbrook to the shire-wide Rudder Park Management Plan modification process' was defeated 2/7. The primary source text is more specific: the amendment proposed absorbing the Bellbrook matter into the existing shire-wide Rudder Park Management Plan modification process - i.e., treating Bellbrook procedurally as an extension of the plan council already has, rather than as a matter requiring its own standalone instrument. By defeating it 2/7, the chamber elected to treat Bellbrook as a standalone operational matter.
determinations: If accurate, this means council's own chamber explicitly considered, and rejected, the procedurally faster path of extending its existing Rudder Park plan to cover Bellbrook - choosing instead a path that required a new, standalone process. This directly complicates AR-001's framing of Rudder Park purely as a positive precedent: on this account, the same instrument was offered as a shortcut for Bellbrook and voted down.
paths.boundary: This detail exists only in the uncorroborated Account Two document (see AR-006, AR-008) - it should be read with the same caution as that account's resolution numbers, not treated as confirmed procedural history.

paths.title: Institutional Impact Footprint — Beyond Residential Properties
analysis: The evidence register's description of camp impact is framed mainly around residential properties. The Hardened Submission Package's primary text states the colony 'occupied public spaces including the local primary school, the police station, the Rural Fire Service station, and residential properties' - three specific civic/institutional sites beyond the residential frame the register summary conveys.
determinations: If accurate, the camp's footprint extends to at least three distinct institutional sites (school, police station, RFS station) in addition to residential properties - a materially wider institutional exposure than 'residential contamination' alone conveys, and directly relevant to the Rural Fire Service's own operational capacity in a fire-prone hinterland community.
paths.boundary: This claim exists only in the Hardened Submission Package - it is not independently corroborated by the harm-accountability document, which names only the school and Main Street bus stop specifically, not the police or RFS stations. Treat as uncorroborated pending confirmation.

paths.title: The Seven-Category Community Harm Catalogue
analysis: The Community Harm and Accountability Record (source for EV-0004 and other items) itemises seven distinct, named categories of documented impact: continuous faecal contamination of backyards, gardens, play equipment, crops and public spaces; noise and odour from the camp operating around the clock across seasons; suppression of local hospitality trade from residents and visitors being unable to use outdoor areas; children unable to use backyards, play equipment and outdoor spaces for ordinary daily activity; Bellbrook Public School requiring additional cleaning and structural shelter to protect students at the bus stop and in the school grounds; the Main Street bus stop requiring physical shielding from droppings; and documented physical, mental and financial stress to residents across the full period.

The register does not currently carry this seven-category breakdown as its own item - it is compressed inside EV-0004's broader description of the letter and this case's general framing of 'community harm.'
determinations: This case has a specific, named harm catalogue in its own source material that has not previously been surfaced as its own analytical unit - each of the seven categories is a distinct, checkable claim (e.g. the school-shelter and bus-stop-shielding items are corroborated by Council's own March 2026 letter, EV-0004; the hospitality-trade and mental/financial-stress items are not independently corroborated by any other document in this case).
paths.boundary: This catalogue comes from operator-authored advocacy material, not an independent survey or council record - two of the seven items (school shelter, bus stop shielding) are corroborated by Council's own letter; the remaining five rest on this document alone.

paths.title: The Seven-Item Institutional Silence Enumeration
analysis: The Community Harm and Accountability Record lists seven specific things that have not been provided to residents following Council's 18 March 2026 letter: (1) any response from NSW DCCEEW; (2) any response from Mid North Coast Local Health District; (3) any confirmation of a grant application - program, amount, date or status; (4) any response from Michael Kemp MP; (5) any timeline for the park hard shelters or bus stop shielding; (6) any outcome from the October 2025 meeting; (7) any commitment to develop a Camp Management Plan for Bellbrook.
determinations: This is a more specific and checkable formulation of AR-011's 'documents activity, discloses no outcome' finding - each of the seven silences is independently verifiable (e.g. a GIPA request could directly test items 1-3 and 6) rather than being one general absence.
paths.boundary: This is the operator's own enumeration of what has not been disclosed - it is a reasonable reading of EV-0004's content, not an independently confirmed audit of council's internal records.

paths.title: The Canopy Degradation Section — Explicitly Not Bellbrook-Specific Evidence
analysis: The Hardened Submission Package's Part 3 describes a four-stage ecosystem degradation sequence (canopy defoliation from weight loading and excrement, structural dieback of roosting trees, loss of thermal protection driving colony expansion, expansion onto adjacent private property) as 'observable in documented case studies of equivalent urban roost sites' - and the source document itself appends an explicit hedge: 'the above represents the documented mechanism in comparable managed sites. Site-specific biological survey data for Bellbrook would strengthen this section as formal evidence.'
determinations: This entire section is self-flagged by its own source document as general ecological mechanism, not a Bellbrook-specific finding - no site survey data for the Bellbrook camp exists anywhere in this case's register. It should not be cited as evidence of what is currently happening to Bellbrook's own canopy, matching the source's own explicit self-limitation.
paths.boundary: Recorded here precisely because it is self-excluded material, matching the overreach-control discipline used throughout this analysis - not to introduce it as a finding, but to document that it exists in the source material and was deliberately not relied on.

paths.title: Level 1/Level 2 Management Actions — Full Primary-Source Detail
analysis: The register's summary of available Level 1/Level 2 actions (EV-0012) is considerably less specific than the Hardened Submission Package's Part 4. Level 1 (pre-approved, no licence required) is described there as: high-pressure cleaning and disinfection of public infrastructure, playground equipment, pathways and park structures; installation of shade sails over play equipment, safety fencing around high-impact roost perimeters, and public health advisory signage; and routine mowing, slashing and weed clearance around roosting vegetation. Level 2 (also pre-approved) is described as: lopping, trimming and pruning of specific branches overhanging residential fences, school boundaries, walking tracks or civic structures; and removal of non-roosting vegetation beneath the canopy to create a buffer 'up to a maximum distance of 30 metres from any occupied residential building.' Welfare-based scheduling conditions (evening trimming after animals depart to forage, avoiding extreme heat and late-stage breeding, notifying wildlife rescue groups) apply to both levels as operational conditions, not prohibitions.
determinations: The specific 30-metre buffer figure and the itemised list of concrete interventions (shade sails, safety fencing, advisory signage, high-pressure disinfection) give AR-012's finding real operational content - these are not abstract 'management actions' but a defined menu council could execute without further licensing.
paths.boundary: The 30-metre figure and the itemised action list appear only in the Hardened Submission Package - like other detail from that document, it has not been checked against the primary Code of Practice text itself (Q-0007, DR-004).

paths.title: The Lodgement Status Contradiction — 'Have Now Been Lodged' vs. Unsigned Templates
analysis: The media pitch document states, in the present perfect tense: 'Formal submissions have now been lodged simultaneously with council, the NSW Minister for the Environment, the State Member for Oxley, the Federal Member for Lyne, the Federal Environment Minister, and the NSW Ombudsman.' This directly asserts completed lodgement. Yet the council-submission letter, the Ombudsman complaint, and the Senator Faruqi letter all carry the identical unsigned placeholder - a blank underscore line followed by 'Resident of Bellbrook NSW 2440' - with no signatory name, date, or evidence of having actually been sent.
determinations: This is a direct internal inconsistency between two pieces of this case's own preserved source material: one document asserts the submissions are already lodged; the documents that would need to be lodged remain in unsigned template form. This case's register currently treats lodgement as simply 'unconfirmed' (Q-0005) - the more precise finding is that one source actively claims completion while the primary documents themselves show no sign of it.
paths.boundary: Does not determine which is accurate - the media pitch could be aspirational/forward-dated drafting, or the templates could be unedited copies retained after signed versions were sent elsewhere. This is exactly the kind of finding a single evidence-register summary compresses away and a primary-source re-read surfaces - recommend a future DFAPTI pass ask the operator directly and log the answer as new evidence or a formal contradiction.

paths.title: The Source Material's Own Self-Identified Evidence Gaps
analysis: The Hardened Submission Package's Part 6 sets out three structured 'evidence collection matrices' the original document proposes for closing gaps in its own record: psychosocial impact and the resolution-outcome gap (daily cleaning logs, property damage records, records of restricted outdoor-space use, resident accounts of the October milestone being missed); canopy destruction and property damage (counts of destroyed/damaged trees, financial estimates of vegetation loss, cleaning costs); and the notice chronology (every verbal and written complaint to council, with dates and reference numbers, and records of unreturned calls).
determinations: These three matrices substantially overlap with, but are more granular than, this case's existing Open Question Register - Q-0006 (health impact) and the community harm items in AR-027 map to Matrix 1; no existing open question specifically covers the property-damage/canopy-destruction data in Matrix 2; and the notice-chronology data in Matrix 3 would materially strengthen AR-009/AR-010's report-back-absence findings if it existed.
paths.boundary: These are the source document's own proposed future data-collection targets, not evidence already in this case's register - none of the specific figures the matrices call for (tree counts, cost estimates, complaint logs) exist in this case currently.

paths.title: Additional Candidate Primary Sources Named in the Source Material
analysis: The Hardened Submission Package's Part 7 lists direct URLs to Kempsey Shire Council's own published documentation, including its Disclosure of Interests Register, a Councillor Certified Disclosure Repository, and a Proactive Information Access Log, alongside the council's flying-fox position page and the Rudder Park plan page already cited elsewhere in this case.
determinations: Three of these five URLs (the two disclosure registers and the proactive information access log) have not been checked by this case at any point across seven runs - they are candidate primary sources for a future DFAPTI evidence-gathering pass, not yet examined.
paths.boundary: DFAPTA does not fetch new evidence - this path names the candidate sources for a future DFAPTI pass to check, it does not check them itself.

paths.title: "Confirmed Minutes" Claimed as Evidence Base and Media Asset — Never Independently Obtained by This Case
analysis: The Community Harm and Accountability Record states its own 'Evidence Base' as: 'Primary sources — Kempsey Shire Council confirmed minutes 2022–2026; Council correspondence 18 March 2026; Macleay Argus reporting 2025; NSW DCCEEW Flying-fox Camp Management Policy 2015; NSW Flying-fox Camp Management Code of Practice 2018; NSW flying fox grants program documentation.' Separately, the Media Pitch's 'What Is Available' section offers journalists 'Primary source documents — council letters, confirmed meeting minutes, council website classification of Bellbrook as a "historic" camp while residents live with an active one.'

Both documents describe possessing, or being able to supply, confirmed/signed council minutes. This case's own disclosure request (DR-001) and CTR-0001 record that the signed confirmed minutes of the 20 May 2025 meeting - the single most disputed meeting in this case - have never been independently obtained or sighted by this investigation across seven runs and two case-creation passes; Council's own site and web.archive.org both blocked automated fetch attempts. Checked against source_register.json before writing this path: no entry there records either document's 'confirmed minutes' claim.
determinations: Two of this case's own operator-supplied source documents each represent themselves as drawing on, or able to supply, 'confirmed' council minutes - a status this case's own frozen record establishes was never actually obtained through any channel available to this investigation. This is a tension between what the case's own source material claims for itself and what the case's own verification record shows, not yet reconciled.
paths.boundary: Does not determine whether the documents' authors hold minutes never shared with this investigation, whether 'confirmed' is used loosely to mean something short of the signed primary record, or whether the claim is aspirational/inaccurate drafting - the same range of explanations AR-034 leaves open for the lodgement-status contradiction. Recommend a future DFAPTI pass ask the operator directly whether signed minutes exist in their possession, distinct from this case's own inability to fetch them independently.

paths.title: "Assessed as Not Feasible" — A Single-Source Claim of an Actual 2022 Determination for Bellbrook
analysis: The Community Harm and Accountability Record's governance timeline states, for July 2022: 'Rudder Park vegetation management completed. East Kempsey receives the shire's first completed flying-fox management outcome. Bellbrook assessed as not feasible for vegetation management. No alternative action initiated for Bellbrook.' This case's evidence register (EV-0002) records only that Council has no completed or draft plan for Bellbrook - an absence. This source line makes a materially different claim: that Council actually assessed Bellbrook for vegetation management around the same time as Rudder Park's completion, and reached a negative determination.

No other document in this case's set mentions any 2022 assessment of Bellbrook, states what was assessed or against what criteria, or gives any basis for a 'not feasible' finding - not even the plain-language fact sheet (SRC-0005) drafted from overlapping material. Checked against source_register.json before writing this path: no entry there records this claim.
determinations: If accurate, this is a materially different fact than the silence this case's register otherwise documents for the period before the community's own May 2025 request: not an absence of any council attention to Bellbrook, but a specific, dated assessment that concluded against action there and was never disclosed to residents. This would complicate AR-001's 'not blocked by unfamiliarity' framing in a different way than AR-025's amendment-defeat finding does - by suggesting a site-specific assessment happened roughly three years before the community's own formal request, not only that the instrument itself was familiar to the council.
paths.boundary: This claim exists only in the Community Harm and Accountability Record - it is not corroborated by the fact sheet drafted from overlapping material (SRC-0005), by council's own March 2026 letter (EV-0004), or by any other document in this case. Should not be read as confirmed council practice, only as a specific single-source claim requiring the same caution this case applies to other uncorroborated detail (see AR-026, AR-031, AR-032). Recommend a future DFAPTI pass ask the operator for the assessment's source or context.

paths.title: The Camp Management Plan as Prerequisite Gateway vs. Parallel Available Action — Two Framings in the Case's Own Primary Sources
analysis: AR-012 and AR-032 describe Level 1 (routine site management) and Level 2 (vegetation buffer) actions, drawn from the Hardened Submission Package's Part 4, as 'pre-approved' and 'not requiring individual licensing or regulatory authorisation' under the Code of Practice - available to council independent of any Camp Management Plan for the site. The Community Harm and Accountability Record initially lists these same actions the same way, as parallel items alongside 'Development of a Flying-fox Camp Management Plan' in a list of things the species-protection constraint does not prevent (its Section 2). But the same document's Section 4 - titled 'The Camp Management Plan — The Decision That Determines Everything Else' - states the Plan 'is the instrument through which... Level 1 and Level 2 actions are documented and authorised without requiring additional licences', and its Section 7 states developing a Plan 'is the gateway to all formal management authority, all grant funding eligibility, and all Level 1 and Level 2 actions under the NSW Code of Practice'. Checked against source_register.json before writing this path: SRC-0006 and SRC-0007's own entries note the Level 1/2 detail and the funding-gating role of a Plan separately, but neither entry records this specific tension between 'available regardless of a plan' and 'available only once a plan exists'.

This is not only a tension between two documents (the Hardened Submission Package's framing vs. the Harm and Accountability Record's Section 4/7 framing) - it recurs inside the Harm and Accountability Record itself, between its own Section 2 (Level 1/2 listed as already-available, parallel to plan development) and Sections 4 and 7 (Level 1/2 described as authorised through the plan).
determinations: AR-012's determination - that legal protection of the species does not by itself explain an absence of interim Level 1/Level 2 action - assumes those actions are available independent of a Camp Management Plan. If the case's own most methodologically careful primary source (SRC-0007, per its own source_register.json entry) is instead read at its Section 4/7 framing, the absence of a Bellbrook plan itself would be a more complete explanation for the absence of Level 1/2 action than AR-012 currently allows for - not a resolution of which framing is correct, but a genuine complication AR-012 and AR-032 do not currently carry.
paths.boundary: Does not determine which framing is correct - the primary Code of Practice text itself (DR-004, Q-0007) is the only source that could resolve whether Level 1/2 actions are genuinely plan-independent or plan-gated, and this case has not yet obtained it. Does not allege the Hardened Submission Package or the Harm and Accountability Record contain a deliberate misstatement - a document written across two sections at different points, using 'available' loosely in one place and 'authorised through the plan' precisely in another, is a plausible innocent explanation this analysis does not rule out. Also does not extend to the wider array of actions Section 2 lists alongside Level 1/2 (infrastructure hardening, resident subsidies, school support, formal advocacy) - this path is scoped to the Level 1/2 pre-approval claim specifically, since that is what AR-012 and AR-032 already treat as established.

paths.title: The November 2019 Bushfire-Refuge Origin — Cross-Corroborated Timing, Single-Source Framing, and an Unanchored Chronology Citation
analysis: The Community Harm and Accountability Record states, in both its narrative introduction (Section 1) and its own governance timeline (Section 3), that the colony 'relocated to Bellbrook during the Black Summer bushfire event' in November 2019 and 'moved into the only unburnt area of the community' to establish its camp. The Media Pitch separately states the colony 'arrived in Bellbrook following the Black Summer fires of November 2019' - corroborating the timing and the bushfire connection independently, in a document drafted for a different purpose (external media outreach rather than an internal accountability record). Neither the Hardened Submission Package, the fact sheet, nor any of the four remaining preserved documents mentions the bushfire origin at all.

The specific 'only unburnt area of the community' refuge detail, however, is not independently corroborated - it appears twice within the single Harm and Accountability Record (its Section 1 introduction and its Section 3 timeline entry for the same document), not in the Media Pitch or anywhere else. This case's own chronology register (CHR-0001) records the origin event as 'Confirmed' status, but cites EV-0001 as its supporting evidence - and EV-0001's own evidence_description concerns the 20 May 2025 council meeting, not the November 2019 origin. No item in this case's evidence register currently anchors the Black Summer/bushfire-refuge origin claim itself. Checked against source_register.json before writing this path: neither SRC-0007's nor SRC-0010's entry records the bushfire-origin detail or this citation gap.
determinations: The camp's arrival timing - November 2019, coinciding with the Black Summer bushfire event - is corroborated across two independently-purposed documents and warrants more confidence than a single-source claim. The specific 'only unburnt area' refuge framing is not independently corroborated (it recurs twice within one document, not across documents) and should be read with the same caution this case applies to other uncorroborated single-document detail (see AR-026, AR-031, AR-032, AR-038) - a distinction this case's register has not previously drawn for this fact.
paths.boundary: Does not allege chronology.json's CHR-0001 citation is erroneous as opposed to merely under-specific, and does not itself correct that citation or mint a dedicated evidence item - both are DFAPTI-level tasks this DFAPTA pass does not perform. Does not establish why the colony specifically selected this site beyond the source material's own stated explanation. Recommend a future DFAPTI pass add a dedicated evidence item anchoring the Black Summer/November 2019 origin claim, distinct from EV-0001, and note whether the 'only unburnt area' detail has any corroboration beyond the Harm and Accountability Record's own restatement of itself. Spot-checked this case's other twelve chronology entries for the same citation-mismatch pattern - all twelve cite evidence items whose own descriptions match the entry's event; CHR-0001 is currently the only instance of this specific gap.

paths.title: Infrastructure Hardening - Listed as Available Regardless of Species Protection, Routed Through a Plan-Gated Funding Mechanism
analysis: The Community Harm and Accountability Record's Section 2 lists 'infrastructure hardening - hard shelters in public spaces, shielded bus stops, covered play equipment' as one of eight actions the species-protection legal constraint (which prevents only dispersal or lethal control) 'does not apply to' - presented alongside Level 1/Level 2 actions, resident subsidies, school support and grant applications as though each were equally available to council independent of that constraint. AR-039's boundary explicitly excluded this wider list from its own scope, treating only the Level 1/Level 2 item.

The same document's own governance timeline (Section 3) and advocacy-chain summary (Section 5) - both underlying EV-0004 - describe council's stated pathway for infrastructure hardening specifically as grant-dependent: the 18 March 2026 letter states only 'plans to seek external grants for park hard shelters and Main Street bus stop shielding', not that hardening work is funded, scheduled, or underway through any other means. No alternative funding source for infrastructure hardening (e.g. existing council budget) is stated anywhere in this document or any other document in this case.

The same document's Section 4 (Finding 4, EV-0011) states the NSW flying-fox grants program requires funding to be directed toward actions in a completed or draft Camp Management Plan, and that Bellbrook has no plan. Checked against source_register.json before writing this path: neither SRC-0007's entry nor SRC-0005's entry records this specific connection between the infrastructure-hardening list item and the plan-gated funding mechanism.
determinations: Section 2's 'does not apply to' framing lists infrastructure hardening as though it were currently actionable independent of a Camp Management Plan, in the same way AR-039 found for Level 1/2 actions. But the only funding pathway this document itself describes for infrastructure hardening - external grants - is, per this same document's own Finding 4 and EV-0011, unavailable to Bellbrook without the very Camp Management Plan council declined to develop in May 2025 (EV-0002). This extends CPO-011's framing-tension pattern to a second, distinct action category on the Section 2 list, rather than resolving whether the Level 1/2 tension itself is real.
paths.boundary: Does not determine whether council could fund infrastructure hardening through a non-grant source (e.g. general council budget) - the source material states only that council's own stated pathway is external grants, not that no other funding route exists; resolving that would require council's own budget records, which this case does not have. Does not extend this specific finding to resident subsidies or formal advocacy, the two Section 2 list items not examined here. School support (the letter to Bellbrook Public School, per Section 5) appears to have already been delivered without a stated dependency on a Plan, so that item's 'available regardless' framing is not contradicted the same way this path questions infrastructure hardening's. Does not allege the Community Harm and Accountability Record's Section 2 list contains a deliberate misstatement - an abstract framework section written without deliberate cross-reference to the same document's own later funding-mechanism analysis is a plausible innocent explanation not ruled out here, matching AR-039's own treatment of the Level 1/2 tension. Does not determine whether the grants program is genuinely the only funding avenue available to council for infrastructure hardening - that sharpens, rather than resolves, Q-0002/DR-003's existing open question.

paths.title: The Operator's Own Registration Email States No Species Assessment Has Ever Been Conducted — Sharper Than This Case's Own 'No Data' Finding
analysis: AR-015 states that this case's own register contains no basis to assess the Bellbrook colony against the EPBC Act's 'nationally important camp' referral threshold - an absence in this case's evidentiary record. EV-0022's own text, the operator's 18 June 2026 email to DCCEEW Species Policy, makes a broader and more specific claim than that absence: it states that no formal species identification, ecological assessment, or census of the Bellbrook colony has been conducted by Kempsey Shire Council, CSIRO, or any government agency at any point since the colony's arrival in approximately November 2019. That is not this case failing to obtain data that exists somewhere - it is a sourced claim, put directly to the responsible Commonwealth department by the operator, that no such assessment exists at all.

This also bears on the welfare-based scheduling conditions attached to the Level 1/Level 2 management actions this case's material otherwise treats as pre-approved and available (AR-012, AR-032, AR-039, AR-041) - conditions such as trimming only after animals depart to forage, or avoiding late-stage breeding, presuppose some basic seasonal or behavioural knowledge of the specific colony to schedule around, which the operator's own claim states has never been formally gathered for this site.
determinations: If accurate, AR-015's open EPBC threshold question is not merely unresolved for lack of this case's own access to existing data - per the operator's own sourced account, no government or institutional body at any level has ever formally assessed this specific colony. This removes 'an assessment exists but has not been disclosed to this investigation' as the likely explanation for AR-015's gap, without establishing what the threshold assessment would find if performed.
paths.boundary: This is a single-source claim from the operator's own email - itself Requires Verification/Unverified under this case's standard classification (see EV-0022) - made to support a census request, not independently confirmed against council, CSIRO or DCCEEW's own records. Does not establish that no internal or informal assessment exists that has simply gone undisclosed to the operator, only that the operator's own account, put directly to DCCEEW, states none is known to have occurred. Does not extend to whether Bellbrook actually meets or fails the EPBC 'nationally important camp' threshold - Q-0011 remains fully open, and this path does not speculate about the likely outcome of an assessment that, on this account, has never been performed.

paths.title: The Community Consultation Output Gap — An Eighth Undisclosed Item Distinct from the Harm and Accountability Record's Own Enumeration
analysis: AR-028 enumerates seven specific things the Community Harm and Accountability Record's own Section 5 states have not been provided to residents following Council's 18 March 2026 letter - each directed at an external body or outcome (DCCEEW's response, Mid North Coast Local Health District's response, grant application confirmation, Michael Kemp MP's response, an infrastructure timeline, the October 2025 meeting outcome, and a Camp Management Plan commitment). None of these seven items concerns what became of the August 2025 community meeting and September 2025 door-to-door visits themselves - the consultation the same document's own governance timeline (Section 3) and advocacy-chain summary (Section 5) state produced 'feedback collected and described as shared with state decision-makers.'

Two of this case's four drafted-but-unconfirmed advocacy documents (AR-021) raise a distinct, more specific claim about that same consultation. The council-submission letter's third question to Council's CEO asks: 'What documents were produced from the August and September 2025 community consultation? To whom were they provided, in what form, and when?' The Ombudsman complaint states this more directly as an item of conduct under investigation: council 'conducted community consultation and failed to produce or disclose any document chain from that process ... in a manner that is misleading to the community that participated.' Both documents treat the absence of any disclosed output from the consultation itself - not merely the absence of a state-agency response to it - as a distinct undisclosed item. Checked against source_register.json before writing this path: SRC-0008's and SRC-0011's own entries record only that each document's account of the May 2025 meeting matches SRC-0001 rather than SRC-0006; neither entry records this specific consultation-output claim, so it is a genuinely new finding, not a re-litigation.
determinations: This case's existing institutional-silence finding (AR-028) is not exhaustive of what this case's own source material identifies as undisclosed - it covers what has not been received back from external bodies, not what has not been returned to the community whose own participation generated the material. If accurate, the August/September 2025 consultation's own output was, on this account, never shared with the people who supplied it, only (per the Harm and Accountability Record's own account) with state decision-makers. This is a distinct, eighth category of undisclosed information, not a restatement of AR-028's existing seven.
paths.boundary: This claim exists only in two of the four drafted-but-unconfirmed advocacy documents (AR-021) - it is a question and an allegation framed within draft correspondence that itself has no confirmed lodgement date (Q-0005), not an independently confirmed fact that no consultation output exists or was withheld. Council may hold a document chain from the consultation that was simply not put before this case, or may have provided informal feedback not captured in written form; this path does not rule either possibility out, matching the same caution AR-011 and AR-028 already apply to Council's own account. Does not allege the omission was deliberate or misleading - it reports that two source documents characterise it that way, without adopting that characterisation as established. Does not propose that council be asked to produce this material or name any recipient for such a request - that is Enforcement Notice/Advocacy Package territory (see DEC-0008); this path states only that the gap exists as a documented claim in this case's own source material and has not previously been captured as its own analytical point.

paths.title: The May 2025 Refusal Decision — Two Documents Note It Has Never Been Reversed
analysis: The Community Harm and Accountability Record's own Finding 3 states, of Council's May 2025 refusal to develop a Camp Management Plan for Bellbrook: 'The decision has not been reversed in any confirmed council record.' Independently, the Facts Insert's own itemised list of what council 'has not' done includes, as its own line item: 'Reversed the May 2025 decision to decline the management plan.' Both documents single this out as a distinct point in its own right, not folded into a general description of plan absence.

This is a different claim from this case's existing 'no plan exists' finding (AR-001, resting on EV-0002 and EV-0017) and from the seven-item institutional-silence enumeration (AR-028). AR-001 and EV-0017 describe an absence - no Bellbrook plan currently exists. AR-028 describes silence about outcomes of later advocacy activity following the March 2026 letter. Neither states, as its own point, that the specific May 2025 refusal itself remains an undisturbed, un-revisited determination - that no later confirmed council action has reopened or reversed that particular decision, as distinct from council simply never having produced a plan by some other route. Checked against source_register.json in full first: neither SRC-0007's entry nor SRC-0005's entry records this specific 'not reversed' framing, so it is a genuinely new finding, not a re-litigation.
determinations: Two independently-purposed case documents - an investigation record and a plain-language public fact sheet, both dated May 2026 - each treat the May 2025 refusal not merely as a past event but as a standing determination that no later confirmed council action has revisited or reversed. This is distinguishable from this case's existing 'no plan exists' finding, which describes an absence rather than the continuing effect of a specific dated decision.
paths.boundary: Does not establish that council has taken no informal or internal step to reconsider the decision - only that no document in this case's register records any reversal, matching the same caution this case applies to other absence-of-record claims (EV-0017, AR-011, AR-028). Does not allege the non-reversal reflects deliberate obstruction or any other motive - both source documents state this as a governance-record fact, not as an inference about intent, and this path does not go further than either does.

paths.title: Six Named 'Simultaneous' Recipients, Two Matching Drafts
analysis: The council-submission letter (EV-0006) states this submission 'is being provided simultaneously to the NSW Minister for Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water; the State Member for Oxley; the Federal Member for Lyne; the Federal Minister for the Environment and Water; and the NSW Ombudsman' - five additional recipients beyond council itself, six in total. The media pitch document - already the subject of AR-034's own lodgement-tense finding - echoes the same six-recipient list, asserting in the present perfect that 'Formal submissions have now been lodged simultaneously with' all six.

Of those six named recipients, this case's preserved material contains an actual drafted submission for only two: the council-submission letter itself (EV-0006, addressed to CEO Andrew Meddle) and the Ombudsman complaint (EV-0007). No draft addressed to the NSW Minister for Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water, the State Member for Oxley, the Federal Member for Lyne, or the Federal Minister for the Environment and Water exists anywhere in this case's preserved material.

A third advocacy draft does exist in this case (the Greens senator letter, SRC-0009), but it is addressed to Senator Mehreen Faruqi, Deputy Leader of the Australian Greens - a recipient not named among the six at all - and its own request is not a direct submission but an ask that she raise the matter with the actual Federal Minister for the Environment and Water via Senate Estimates. Checked source_register.json in full first: SRC-0008's, SRC-0009's and SRC-0011's own entries each describe their respective single recipient and draft status individually, and none cross-references the other two or notes that the six-recipient list named inside SRC-0008's own text has a matching draft for only two of its six names, so this is a genuinely new finding, not a re-litigation.
determinations: The six-recipient 'simultaneous' submission claim, already shown by AR-034 to assert completed lodgement against unsigned templates, carries a second and independent layer of imprecision: this case's own material has no corresponding drafted document for four of the six named recipients, and the one additional draft beyond the two that do match is addressed to a recipient outside the named six. The claim describes a more coordinated advocacy effort than this case's own document set currently supports.
paths.boundary: Does not determine that submissions to the four unmatched recipients were never made - only that no corresponding document exists in this case's preserved material or evidence register; the operator may hold drafts or records not yet supplied to this case, the same distinction this case already applies to 'not sighted' versus 'does not exist' (Q-0003, DR-001). Does not allege the council-submission letter or media pitch overstated this deliberately - a plausible innocent explanation is that copies were drafted and sent without being retained in this case's material, or that the six-recipient list described an intention not yet fully executed at the time of drafting. Sharpens, rather than resolves, Q-0005. Does not propose that any of the four unmatched recipients be asked for a response or otherwise contacted - see DEC-0008. Separately notes, without correcting it, that SRC-0009 is the only one of this case's eight preserved primary-source documents with no evidence_register.json entry of its own - a gap in this case's evidence base logged here as a candidate future DFAPTI item, not something this DFAPTA pass corrects.

paths.title: The Attached Record's Own Date vs. Three Letters' Citation of It
analysis: The Community Harm and Accountability Record (EV-0004's source, SRC-0007) states its own preparation date on its face: 'Prepared: May 2026'. Three separate advocacy drafts - the council-submission letter (EV-0006), the NSW Ombudsman complaint (EV-0007), and the Greens senator letter (SRC-0009) - each independently list, in an identical attachment line, 'Bellbrook Flying Fox — Community Harm and Accountability Record, June 2026'. All three letters are themselves dated June 2026 on their own letterheads, but the document they describe attaching is not: it is the same document this case's own source register already dates 'Bellbrook Flying-Fox Harm and Accountability Record, May 2026' (SRC-0007's own title).

This is not a single slip in one letter - the identical one-month mismatch recurs across all three independently-addressed drafts (to council, the Ombudsman, and a federal senator), each restating the record's title with its own letter's month rather than the record's actual self-stated month. Checked against source_register.json in full first: SRC-0006's, SRC-0007's, SRC-0008's, SRC-0009's and SRC-0011's own entries each describe their own document individually and none records this specific date mismatch between the record's self-dating and how the three letters cite it, so this is a genuinely new finding, not a re-litigation.
determinations: Every drafted document in this case that cites the Community Harm and Accountability Record by date names it 'June 2026', a month later than the record's own stated preparation date of 'May 2026' - a consistent, three-times-repeated discrepancy between how the record identifies itself and how it is identified by the correspondence built on it.
paths.boundary: Does not determine which date is accurate, or whether a distinct June 2026 revision of the record exists that this case's preserved material does not carry - the simplest explanation is that all three June-dated letters were drafted from a template restating each letter's own month rather than checking the attachment's actual title, which this path does not rule out as the likely cause. Does not allege the mismatch was deliberate, or that the attached document differs in substance from the one this case has preserved - only that the title used to cite it is not the title the document gives itself. This is the same kind of internal-consistency check DEC-0009/DEC-0010 established as standing practice - checked here against source_register.json before being treated as a finding, and found not already recorded there.

cross_path_observations.title: The plan mechanism is demonstrated, not exotic
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-001, AR-003 and AR-004 converge: the management-plan instrument is actively operated inside Kempsey Shire itself (Rudder Park), actively revised by a comparable regional council (Townsville), and specifically funded for development elsewhere (Mount Isa). No single path alone shows all three; together they remove 'this is a rare or unfunded mechanism' as an available explanation for Bellbrook's absence of one.

cross_path_observations.title: Three accounts, three different evidentiary weights
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-005, AR-006, AR-007 and AR-008 together show the meeting-account dispute is not a simple two-sided contradiction - it is three accounts with three distinct sourcing profiles, only one of which (AR-006) supplies the specific numbers this case's strongest remedy language would need, and that one is also the least corroborated.

cross_path_observations.title: The report-back gap has a confirmed core and an unconfirmed extension
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-009 and AR-010 together show this case should not treat 'no report-back through February 2026' as a single fact of uniform confidence - the October 2025 absence is cross-source confirmed; the extension through November, December and February is currently single-source.

cross_path_observations.title: One Commonwealth channel, two distinct open questions
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-013, AR-014 and AR-015 together show the Commonwealth registration attempt produced one hard confirmed fact (the program's pause) and left one genuinely separate question open (the EPBC threshold) - these should not be treated as a single resolved 'Commonwealth pathway is dead' finding.

cross_path_observations.title: Three independent strands, no single conclusive one
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-016, AR-017 and AR-018 each bear on whether Bellbrook's camp is accurately described as 'historic' - a partially-corroborated classification claim, an unlocated severity report, and a confirmed real 2021 departure that could fully explain the classification without inaccuracy. No single strand is conclusive; read together they show why CTR-0002 remains genuinely, not just formally, open.

cross_path_observations.title: Two health mechanisms, not one 'health risk' finding
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-019 and AR-020 are structurally distinct risks (fungal, droppings-borne vs. viral, bite/scratch-borne) that a less granular pass would have compressed into a single generic 'health risk exists' path - keeping them separate preserves the different evidentiary bases each actually has.

cross_path_observations.title: One confirmed action stands apart from four unconfirmed drafts
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-013 and AR-021 together show this case's advocacy record is not a uniform set of 'things the operator tried' - one action (Commonwealth registration) has a confirmed send date and a confirmed reply; four drafted channels (council, Ombudsman, and two more referenced in the same drafting round) remain unconfirmed. Conflating them would overstate what has actually been attempted - and AR-034 shows one source document actively asserts they were sent while the drafts themselves show no sign of it.

cross_path_observations.title: Primary-source re-reading surfaces what register summaries compress away
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-024 through AR-036 exist only because Pass 2 went back to the eight preserved primary documents directly rather than relying on evidence_register.json's own condensed descriptions. The most significant single finding of this pass - AR-034's lodgement-status contradiction - was invisible in Pass 1 precisely because the register's EV-0006/EV-0007 summaries describe the drafts' content, not the tension between the media pitch's completion claim and the drafts' own unsigned state. The three-way colony-continuity discrepancy (AR-024) is the same pattern: a real inconsistency that exists in the frozen source material regardless of which pass reads it, but that only a close primary-source read surfaces.

cross_path_observations.title: The case's most specific detail and its most cautious sourcing share one document
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-006 (the specific resolution numbers), AR-025 (the defeated Rudder Park absorption amendment), AR-031 (the self-excluded canopy-degradation section) and AR-032's most specific detail (the 30-metre buffer figure) all originate in the single least-corroborated document in this case, the Hardened Submission Package. This is not a reason to discount them individually - each stands or falls on its own terms - but the concentration is itself worth naming: this case's most granular procedural and technical detail and its most evidentially cautious material are the same document.

cross_path_observations.title: The claims-vs-record gap pattern recurs a third time
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-006 (the Hardened Submission Package's specific resolution numbers, uncorroborated elsewhere), AR-034 (the media pitch's 'have now been lodged' claim against the drafts' own unsigned state), and AR-037 (two documents' own 'confirmed minutes' claims against this case's inability to obtain them through any channel) are three separate instances of the same underlying pattern: a document in this case's own source material asserting a more complete or more certain state of affairs than this case's independently-verifiable record supports. No single instance establishes bad faith or error on its own - each has its own boundary and a plausible innocent explanation this analysis does not rule out - but the recurrence across three distinct documents and three distinct claims is itself worth naming as a pattern future passes on this case should watch for.

cross_path_observations.title: The Level 1/2 finding has an unresolved framing tension underneath it
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-012 and AR-032 treat Level 1/Level 2 management actions as available to council independent of a Camp Management Plan - the basis for AR-012's determination that legal species-protection does not by itself explain the absence of interim action at Bellbrook. AR-039 shows the same primary source material also contains, in the same document and in the same section that most authoritatively states the Plan's role, a description of the Plan itself as the authorising 'gateway' for those same Level 1/2 actions - a framing AR-012 and AR-032 do not currently carry, and which would complicate their determination if accurate. This does not overturn AR-012 or AR-032 - it names an unresolved tension between two readings of the same case material that only surfaces when different sections of the same document are read against each other, and that the primary Code of Practice text (DR-004) is needed to resolve.

cross_path_observations.title: The 'lodged' claim fails on two independent grounds, not one
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-034 shows the documents that would need to be lodged remain unsigned templates. AR-045 shows that, setting signature status aside, this case's material contains a matching drafted document for only two of the six recipients the claim names. Read together, the six-recipient 'simultaneously lodged' claim in the media pitch and the council-submission letter is unsupported by this case's own document set on two independent grounds - lowering, rather than raising, confidence that Q-0005 will resolve toward 'already sent'.

disclosure_requests.title: Signed confirmed minutes, 20 May 2025 Kempsey Shire Council ordinary meeting
disclosure_requests.request: The primary record needed to resolve CTR-0001 and Q-0001 - which of the three accounts (AR-005, AR-006, AR-007) is accurate, including whether Resolution 2025.79/2025.80 and the stated 9/0 vote and defeated 2/7 amendment are real.

disclosure_requests.title: Current text of Council's flying-fox webpage
disclosure_requests.request: A dated, directly-sighted capture of the page's full text - the 'historic' classification, the Rudder Park comparison, and the private/Crown land management claims - needed to resolve Q-0004, Q-0009 and CTR-0002.

disclosure_requests.title: NSW Government flying-fox camp management grants program guidelines
disclosure_requests.request: The program's own published eligibility terms, to confirm or correct the operator-supplied claim analysed in AR-002 that a completed or draft Camp Management Plan is a strict funding precondition. AR-041 (Pass 6) adds a further specific question this same guidance would resolve: whether the plan-gating rule applies to infrastructure-hardening grant categories (park shelters, bus stop shielding) the same way it applies to the vegetation-management grants EV-0011 was originally drawn from, or whether a separate, non-plan-gated funding route exists for hardening works.

disclosure_requests.title: NSW Flying-fox Camp Management Code of Practice 2018 (primary text)
disclosure_requests.request: To confirm the Level 1/Level 2 management actions described in AR-012 against the Code's actual text, including whether Level 1/Level 2 actions require a completed or draft Camp Management Plan as a prerequisite or are available regardless of one - the tension AR-039 identifies between different sections of this case's own source material.

contradictions_preserved.issue: Three distinct accounts of the 20 May 2025 council meeting remain in tension - see AR-005 through AR-008 for the full triangulation.
contradictions_preserved.analysis: Not resolved by this analysis - the signed confirmed minutes have not been obtained across seven runs and two case-creation passes.

contradictions_preserved.issue: Council's current 'historic' classification may or may not match a functional 2026 reality of severe, ongoing impact - see AR-016 through AR-018 for the three independent strands bearing on this, and AR-024 for a related, separate three-way discrepancy over when the colony was actually present.
contradictions_preserved.analysis: Not resolved by this analysis - the June 2026 report has not been located and it is not established whether the colony returned after its confirmed 2021 departure, or whether the Hardened Submission Package's uncited December 2019 start date and mid-2022 return describe the same event or a different history again.

overreach_controls: No claim is made about why Kempsey Shire Council has not produced a Bellbrook-specific management plan - only that it has not, against a mechanism it operates elsewhere in the same shire.
No intent is attributed to any individual councillor, council officer, or Commonwealth official at any point in this analysis - every finding describes documented institutional record, not motive.

AR-006 and AR-008 do not adopt the Hardened Submission Package's characterisation of council's conduct as non-execution of an affirmative unanimous directive - that characterisation depends on the unresolved CTR-0001 and is not treated as established here.

AR-016 through AR-018 do not present the 'historic' classification as inaccurate or as a confirmed documented-vs-functional gap - CTR-0002 remains genuinely open, with a real alternative explanation (the 2021 departure, AR-018) not yet ruled out.

AR-019 and AR-020 do not claim any Bellbrook resident has experienced histoplasmosis or an ABLV exposure - both are stated as real mechanisms without a confirmed local instance, matching the source evidence's own explicit hedge.

AR-031 and AR-032 do not adopt the 30-metre buffer figure or any other Hardened Submission Package detail as confirmed - both originate in the least-corroborated document in this case (see CPO-009) and are presented as candidate material, not established findings.

AR-031 explicitly excludes the Hardened Submission Package's canopy-degradation section from this case's evidentiary basis, matching that section's own self-declared limitation - it is documented here as existing in the source material, not relied upon.

AR-024 and AR-034 name real inconsistencies in this case's own frozen source material without resolving them or assuming which side of each is accurate - resolving them is a DFAPTI-level task (confirming facts, obtaining the operator's clarification) that this DFAPTA pass does not perform. A third apparent inconsistency (originally AR-023, an advocate named 'Paul Hodgson' in five documents and 'Paul Hodgkinson' in one) was removed 2026-08-25 (DEC-0009) - this is a single-document spelling variant, not a genuine unresolved discrepancy, and treating it as one overstated a trivial transcription artefact as material uncertainty. Correct verification practice recognises and normalises an obvious variant against five consistent references rather than preserving it as an open question.

This analysis does not propose remedies, recipients, or submission strategies for any finding - a SafeWork NSW/Work Health and Safety Act theory and an Office of Local Government NSW submission pathway (originally AR-029, AR-030) and a sixth advocacy channel to Senator Faruqi (originally AR-033) were removed 2026-08-25 after the operator flagged that Advocacy Package-only content - remedies sought, recipients, what to ask them for - had been run through the analysis gate (DEC-0008). DFAPTA states what the evidence and source material show; who to send it to and what to ask for belongs to Enforcement Notice and Advocacy Package, neither of which exists yet.

This pass deliberately does not compress distinct claims of different evidentiary weight into single generic findings (see AR-022, CPO-006, CPO-007 and CPO-008) - the original nine-path pass's central failure was doing exactly that, and is not repeated here.

AR-037 and CPO-010 do not allege any document's claims-vs-record gap was made in bad faith or deliberately - each has a plausible innocent explanation (loose use of 'confirmed', aspirational drafting, or a record-keeping oversight) that this analysis does not rule in or rule out. AR-038 does not allege council concealed a 2022 assessment - only that if the single source describing one is accurate, it was never disclosed to residents in any document this case has sighted.

AR-039 does not determine whether Level 1/Level 2 management actions genuinely require a Camp Management Plan as a legal prerequisite or are available regardless of one - it names a framing tension inside the case's own primary source material (including within a single document) that only the primary Code of Practice text itself (DR-004) can resolve, and does not treat either framing as established over the other.

AR-040 does not allege chronology.json's CHR-0001 citation was corrupted or altered - only that it currently references an evidence item whose own description concerns a different event, a gap this pass identifies but does not correct, since chronology.json is a DFAPTI-level frozen file this analysis does not modify.

AR-041 does not determine whether council has, or lacks, any funding route for infrastructure hardening other than the plan-gated grants program - only that the one pathway this case's source material itself describes is plan-gated. It does not extend the Section 2 'available regardless' critique to resident subsidies or formal advocacy, which this path does not examine.

AR-042 does not allege DCCEEW, CSIRO or Kempsey Shire Council has concealed an existing assessment - it reports the operator's own sourced claim, made to DCCEEW directly, that no such assessment is known to have occurred, and does not treat that claim as independently confirmed.

AR-043 does not allege the August/September 2025 consultation's output was deliberately withheld or that no document chain exists - it reports that two draft advocacy documents characterise the absence that way, without adopting that characterisation as established, and does not propose that council be asked to produce the material or name any recipient for such a request (see DEC-0008).

AR-044 does not allege the May 2025 decision's non-reversal reflects deliberate obstruction, bad faith, or any other motive - it reports that two source documents state this as a governance-record fact, and does not treat 'not reversed in any confirmed record' as proof no internal reconsideration has occurred.

AR-045 does not allege submissions to the four unmatched recipients were never made, and does not allege the council-submission letter or media pitch overstated the six-recipient claim deliberately - it reports a document-coverage gap in this case's own preserved material, not a finding about what actually happened outside that material, and does not propose contacting any of the four unmatched recipients (see DEC-0008).

AR-046 does not determine which of the two dates (the record's own 'May 2026' or the three letters' 'June 2026') is accurate, and does not allege the mismatch was deliberate or that a substantively different document is at issue - it names a repeated citation discrepancy in this case's own preserved material, matching the same caution AR-024 and AR-034 apply to other internal inconsistencies, and does not propose any correction or recipient action (see DEC-0008).

This is Pass 11 of an explicitly ongoing process. It is not represented as exhaustive relative to future passes, and no downstream stage should be built from it until the operator states DFAPTA itself is frozen.
